newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany mulls tax on hidden reserves at utilities.
newsitem.headline: Germany mulls tax on hidden reserves at utilities.

text.p: German state finance ministers are expected to meet later this week to decide on a proposal to tax the hidden reserves of utilities, a move that could cost power firms up to three billion marks, a news magazine reported.

A report to appear in the Monday edition of Der Spiegel magazine said German utilities could end up paying between 1.5 and three billion marks in taxes on an estimated 45 billion marks in reserve to pay for mothballing nuclear power plants.

A spokeswoman for the Bonn finance ministry said in response to Reuters enquiries that in question were tax liabilities for around seven billion marks that the companies put in reserve for operating costs of a nuclear waste dump in Gorleben.
But any tax liability would not affect the entire sum, but rather only the interest earned on the amount, she said, but declined to comment on the expected sum to be paid.
According to Der Spiegel, the companies plan to challenge the move in court.
